Overall a negative review. The BGM rhythm isn’t clear enough, so you have to stare at the rhythm bar to hit the beats correctly. Hitting the beats precisely doesn’t give any special rewards or feedback — even a full-just rhythm only gives one character a pitiful 10% damage boost, with no special sound effects or animations. Because you’re forced to keep staring at the rhythm bar, it gets boring very quickly. comparing with patapon 3， a full-just command will make ur hero to commence special skills with obvious light and sound effects. Skills look good, sound good, and deal a lot of damage or heal or something else, with this feedback, u will automatically try to stick to the rhythm. But ratatan, as a music game, gives no feedback at all for just command (if 10% damage is a meaningful reward>_9 )

当前版本不推荐，patapon老玩家入手需极度谨慎，反而是对这类感兴趣的新玩家可以考虑蹲一下（但依旧不推荐现在入手）。 想现在入手尝试的玩家，需要了解以下几点： 1：非纯节奏游戏，操作模式采用摇杆/方向键+节奏键的模式，同时还存在英雄独立跳跃键，也就是你需要自主控制英雄角色移动跳跃的同时打节奏，导致本作更像轻微横板动作混节奏音乐。我玩到第四关感觉甚至有的时候走位比打准节奏更重要。 2：纯粹的，带轻肉鸽的纯刷子游戏。且当前版本下，为线性游戏。无法选关，每次死亡只能从第一关开始打。 游戏流程基本就是，打怪→打不过→刷装备/素材→升级武器/技能树→再打怪，循环。 打多几遍之后会觉得很无聊，即使你死在第五关，武器装备已经挺不错的了，前几关简单的小怪和boss即使能几下打死，也都要每次再打一遍才行。虽然游戏内提供了一定程度的跳关选项，但是每一大关至少也得刷几关小怪和尾王才能过。 而且更可怕的是当前能构筑的东西非常少，一眼看到底。 3：当前版本几乎不存在剧情。 4：patapon玩家上来可能会对这游戏节奏很不习惯，不论是奇怪的空拍还是每小关之间的间断都会让人很别扭。适应几小时后说实话感觉其实还好，但我依然会觉得这整个操作模式很诡异。 5：画面颜色混乱辨识度低，容易疲劳。经常打着打着找不到控制的英雄跑哪里了，尤其是一些敌方远程攻击，在乱七八糟打起来之后，完全看不出敌人飞行物在哪。对，说的就是丛林关那个会tm射黄色抛物线跳弹的玩意儿，打中极疼，打的时候又经常看不清。 ============================== 这游戏我蹲了很久，只能说现在的状态让人失望。即使我想更客观的评价，也很难说不去和patapon做对比。但好笑的是，写到这边我觉得其实也不用去和patapon对比了，因为除了一点画风，一部分游戏模式类似之外，其他基本都不一样。 游戏最怕的就是无聊，而这游戏当前版本相当无聊。 我不知道我打了几个小时的游戏目的是什么，为了往前多推进一点看看关底boss长什么样？还是为了多刷点小垃圾回来合成升级一下？我能打4个多小时的原因是我还抱着，打通这几关之后可能就会有新模式，新的地图，新的东西的想法。实际这就已经是全部了。 我是期望这游戏能更有趣，更好玩的。但是还是那句话，即使我知道现在是个ea版，即使我尽量放低了要求，现在这个版本依旧是不合格，不推荐的。 PS：联机模式我觉得是很有开发潜力的，真心希望后续开发能跟上吧，唉…等之后更新了再来看是否改成推荐。 ========================== 不知道是BUG还是什么：我桌面上的游戏图标是个白方块，跟没刷出来一样，挺神奇。

如果你是想玩打节奏类型的游戏，那你要失望了，这是个数值游戏 我老老实实敲节奏，对面根本不管节奏直接打我，小兵这样就算了，那些有蓄力前摇的高伤怪就很过分 道中的怪基本上是我敲节奏-看到对面出前摇-我想敲节奏应对-我还没敲完节奏就被打 更是有些前摇出来一两秒就打的，根本不给你时间 boss也是，boss的很多攻击都是卡着我防御或者跳跃动作出来的那一瞬间打出来，还是有概率会被打中，有种讲武德但是又不是很想讲武德的感觉 有个兵种的技能是挡住弹幕，但是这个技能动作有个前摇，前摇结束之前boss的弹幕就已经糊脸上了 这个游戏的我方角色分啦嗒铛和歌宝两种单位，玩家可以直接自由操纵啦嗒铛行动，啦嗒铛本身没有作战能力，可以指挥歌宝是战斗，打节奏指令指挥歌宝集结到啦嗒铛的近右方，也可以让歌宝在当前位置进攻还是防守等等 啦嗒铛血量归零就会游戏失败，歌宝血量归零会暂时离场，过一段时间复活，只要啦嗒铛不死，歌宝能无限回场 boss和部分的一些攻击会直接盯着啦嗒铛打，还有些弹幕非常恶心，你要躲避这种攻击，但是有个问题，【玩家在敲节奏的时候啦嗒铛是无法行动的】，也就是说会出现要专心操作啦塔铛躲避攻击导致无法敲节奏空过的情况，啦塔铛的机动性又很难躲开那些逆天弹幕，最后就变成断指令忙活半天还是被扣血 整体玩下来给我的感觉就是，唯一解是堆数值，因为敌人根本不看你节奏，不想跟你互动 但是游戏又要我以打节奏的方式给歌宝输入指令，但是敌人又不管我节奏，就 感觉这个打节奏的玩法跟游戏是割裂的 不如干脆直接一个键和组合键指挥作战好像还更好玩点 肉鸽要素也令人费解 有一个叫啦嗒牌的局内装备系统 毒、火、冰的套装效果以及部分牌的效果是在啦嗒铛的附近生成攻击特效 但是这个游戏的玩法就是要极力避免啦嗒铛死亡 套装效果有十几秒的cd还没伤害，感觉就是凑数的 不是很懂设计的想法

[h2] 前景提要：作为PataPon系列死忠粉的我尽管在Demo就觉得有诸多问题，但依旧还是管不住首发购入的小手，最远进度是开了女神恶作剧的世界5Boss（相当于用亚种&其他更强？的龙系Boss替换掉基础的版本，细化到世界5Boss则是打完一条血会变身），目前的抢先体验版实在不能昧着良心推荐，下面将列出我玩到现在的个人主观不适点，也算是给还在观望的系列死忠粉打个预防针吧 [/h2] [h3] 首先是依旧贫瘠混乱的局内构筑 [/h3] 作为一个肉鸽游戏，Ratatan的局内构筑属实太贫瘠，这点在Demo我就有指出过了，然而抢先体验版依旧没能改进这个问题，下面我来介绍一下本作的局内构筑系统：游戏中的主要成长点卡牌一共有火、水、风、冰、毒五种属性，而这些卡牌有两个通用的效果就是给普通or技能攻击附魔（各自只能选择一种属性，例如不存在给普攻附魔火+风的情况，后者会覆盖前者），另外有一部分卡牌则是强化各自附魔攻击的效果（例如火属性点燃可以短时间恐惧敌方小兵，水属性浪花增加伤害&击退且被浪花打死的敌方单位会再生成浪花等等，然而此类卡牌并不多，不存在一种属性攻击被强化到登峰造极的情况，大部分时候只会演变成简单的稀有度替换），最后每种属性也有各自不同的侧重点的常规加成卡牌（例如火是侧重低血量增伤加抗&各类烧血增伤，水是各类护盾，毒是对Boss伤害），而每种属性卡集齐一定数量则会给主角带来额外的伤害手段（属性环绕物、间歇性喷毒球、间歇性旋风，不过注意常规情况主角是无法攻击的，你只能移动跳跃躲避&用指令操纵歌宝战斗）当然还有一个主角血量上限的成长，不过一般不太会选就是了，而主角操纵的歌宝在局内是有控制上限的，对比有类似成长逻辑的黑帝斯（卡牌对应了神祇，也有类似半人马之心的加血上限道具）Ratatan的局内构筑属实不甚理想，卡牌的出现顺序也十分混乱，三选一经常是攻击附魔还没获得就莫名出了后续强化该附魔的卡牌，还有明明我自己已经构筑了一套以某个属性攻击为核心的打法，却莫名给出稀有度更低的另一属性攻击附魔，每局的构筑可以说是大同小异，都是清一色的某个属性攻击+对应属性攻击强化+大把其他各类属性的加成效果+偶尔加点血上限，这就导致了本作作为一个肉鸽重玩价值寥寥，玩家几乎没法通过在每局试验不同构筑来获得更多乐趣，我寻思为啥不给跳跃&防御也设置某个卡牌属性效果呢？另外为啥不能模仿黑帝斯的锤子在局内给歌宝升级改变攻击模组呢？ [h3] 其次是乏善可陈的局外成长 [/h3] 我并不反对在肉鸽中加入武器打造升级&随机词条，也不反对学习黑帝斯的夜之圣镜系统（这部分真的既视感满满），但你要学也学全啊，咋改变肉鸽内环境的承包商完全没有啊？目前体验下来只有给每个世界设置回血泉水，其余涉及到环境or收益的是一点没有啊，歌宝也是只能升级数量上限&可编辑数量，那么多角色唯一的区别点就只有血量&移速&蚊子腿光环效果&初期可携带的歌宝职业（Demo后期可以升级解锁歌宝职业以供全角色携带，结果神TM抢先体验版要用特定角色通一次世界5才能解锁），为啥不做个类似技能树的升级系统呢？例如可以让每个角色通过点技能强化自己初始携带的歌宝职业，点满则可以继承到其他角色身上，另外光环也可以加点强化&进一步解锁不同效果的分支，现在这个局外成长真就是味如嚼蜡，武器只能做一次，多余的材料只能积灰，每每重新走一遍世界1-5只能搬点狗粮+个位数的糖&甜甜圈，属实无聊 [h3] 最后是战斗策略性的严重缺失 [/h3] 作为Patapon的精神续作，Ratatan的策略性在抢先体验版本依旧不让人满意，尽管改进了击飞机制值得表扬，前两个Demo出现过的Boss也还算合理，至少每招每式都固定了出招拍子有对应的手段化解，但世界3的Boss就有点莫名了，不会后退一直压缩玩家的行动空间不说，二阶段还会有覆盖所有空间的蓝火&极难躲避的雷球，纯纯的输出检测器，而世界4的Boss则是走位+输出双重检测器，飞鱼&开花冰球那个覆盖范围简直就是小型东方，更别提那个全屏的龙卷风完全无法规避只能硬吃，输出不够就只能被活活耗死，偏偏这Boss还会瞬移+召小弟+拉冰墙，最后是纯纯用来掩盖内容量不足的超绝世界5Boss，各种不讲道理的弹幕+全屏伤害，二阶段还会召唤攻击时刻锁定主角的飞行窗户怪&又臭又硬的南瓜头+弗兰肯斯坦，突出的就是一个强行拉长游玩时间逼着你刷狗粮（甚至我已经升满了三把传奇武器了，卡牌也是水属性加成满&其他杂七杂八buff一大堆，血量也破了500！初见依旧两条命过不了！），只能说策略层面真的是远远不如前作 [h2] 总结一下Ratatan的确有继承PataPon的部分韵味，歌宝辨识度虽然不及简笔的眼球仔，却也依旧十分可爱，但在游玩部分并没有很好得将肉鸽玩法和本家的节奏策略要素融合，故实在不推荐现在入手，感兴趣的系列粉丝我这里建议观望一下，至少也要等到第一波内容更新后再下决定，届时我也会跟进体验后更新评测[/h2]

I want to like this game a lot more than I do right now. The presentation is very charming and bosses are quite interesting, especially with how they play into the separation of the movement of your character and that of your minions to great effect. But unfortunately the regular combat; which is most of what you'll be doing, is about as deep as a puddle and horrendously confused in it's design. I've gotten to the world 5 boss and this game reminds me a lot of Patapon 3. A game where you have barely any agency as a player, and all that really matters is whatever meta progression you've accrued. The basic gist of combat is that you give your units a command, then wait an equal amount of time and give them another one after they've executed it. Bosses interact with this very meaningfully by either having tells one or two command cycles before they execute the attack, or they act based on pattern. Do two command cycles of nothing, then do an untelegraphed move that you have to learn and remember. It's good stuff. Regular combat unfortunately throws this completely out of the window. The majority of enemies are not only completely desynced from the command cycle, but also from each other leading to most encounters being a sequence where your only option is to wildly spam attack and hope they die before you do. This is especially egregious when you have multiple enemies which each in theory wants you to respect them by placing high damage attacks indicated by ground markers, but if you were to try to interact with them at all you would be doing nothing but defending every command cycle making no progress since unlike Patapon, defending makes your ranged units sit completely idle as well. The way that health is handled is also incredibly bizarre. Outside of playing a specific character, there is no means to heal in combat. Rather, every single time your minions die they respawn at half health a while later. The game seems to think that it's like Hades. "Oh, you could buy a potential damage upgrade or you could get some healing for safety, wink wink!" But since damage is largely completely unavoidable it's an utter waste of money. The only time you will be full HP is at the start of any given level making the traits that activate at 75%+ HP almost useless. Thereby you are mostly stuck in a loop where your cobun are killed, respawn at half health and then die immediately before they're able to take action unless you have sufficient meta progression or managed to do enough damage to the encounter before the death cascade began. Variety is also not the strongest suit of Ratatan at time of writing. Every run has you do the same levels, in the same order, fighting the same bosses and pretty much the same overall encounters along the way. And whilst the ones that function within the combat system are fun, it does get rather repetitive. The upgrades that you get on a run also largely don't change how you play, which I think is a shame since I see a lot of potential ways for that to be interesting, and that change of core gameplan is by far my largest enjoyment with roguelikes. To throw out some ideas: What if a trait made it so blocking also made the ratatan attack for free but it had a cooldown. Blocking makes your next attack or special do extra damage. Singing next to units heal them. Whilst moving with the reposition command they deal contact damage to enemies. A unique slot that holds special traits that give you a new song that gives a buff. Just anything instead of "special attack until I'm out of mana, and then regular attack" Short list of other suggestion: Give the base cobun a bit of the stats of the weapons, a low level epic immediately doubling the HP of them makes the early game feel horrendous. Please give us a song to forcibly revive cobun so we don't just have sit around and twiddle our thumbs when we're struck by your meta-centric design. The opportunity cost is already enough of a punishment, since if you were able you'd spend that turn attacking. Even if you made it take two command cycles to execute like jumped worked in the demo it would still feel a lot better than just having to wait. So to summarize, if you just want to play a chill game with charming presentation then absolutely go for it. If you're looking for something that's mechanically coherent, definitely skip it for now.

First of all, I love the concept of the game (especially as a fan of patapon) and I do understand that it is in early access so there's room for improvement. My initial impression of the game was really good, but after some time the cracks began to show. I feel there are some fundamental issues with the game that are holding it back from a truly fun, worthwhile experience. So far I have done around 15 runs (yet to beat a single one, more on that later..), and every single one has felt the same. There is no build expression or smart decision making, it's pretty obvious which choices are the "best" every time and towards the end of a run you will have 95% exactly the same cards as you did every other run. Couple this with the fact that the levels are essentially the exact same each time and you quickly realise that the game is a simple grind to unlock meta progression, which is honestly the biggest issue I have with the game. The game doesn't really care about how "good" you are at playing, you are instead entirely gated behind meta progression. Every successful roguelike that has a meta progression system will put skill expression first, meaning pretty much every successful roguelike will let you clear a run if you have mastered the system with little to no investment in the meta progression systems. Ratatan however demands that you grind out epic/legendary weapons or the loot to craft them, that you grind out other loot drops in order to level those weapons up, that you grind out currency to give you and your units some basic survivability, grind out currency just so you can field x amount of Cobuns. After all this grinding, you can finally beat the world 5 boss and earn the luxury of skill expression of mix and matching your unit composition.. Unfortunately I haven't even managed to beat this boss because I made the stupid mistake of equally upgrading all of the available weapon types instead of maxing a single category. By the time I get to boss 5, my Cobuns do nowhere near enough damage to the massive HP pools of the boss or regular enemies and since boss 5 regularly summons in large enemies the fight just becomes an impossible battle of attrition. Even with perfect card luck, they are essentially just multipliers of your base damage further increasing the need to grind out weapon levels. But you need to beat the boss using every character to have full customisation of course, which means you have to grind out almost every weapon category to stand a chance. It's just layers and layers of grinding. If this system stays as is, the game will never truly be "fun" but just a long slog of grinding out gear until the challenge becomes trivial. Player skill never really matters after a certain point, as long as you keep your Ratatan out of danger you will always be able to grind a boss down if your gear is good enough. Which brings me to another point, the Ratatan character concept is kinda rough. Hero units in games are usually your star unit and your minions act as a support to help them shine. In Ratatan, your hero unit is a liability as your run is entirely dependent on their survival and they don't even attack. It doesn't feel like the devs had a solid direction in mind here either, since a lot of card effects give your Ratatan bonuses for being close to enemies but the effects are so pathetic in comparison to a single Cobun (since there's no scaling nor gear for Ratatans) that by playing the "intended way" you are making the game far harder for yourself than if you were to just stand far away in a safe place. I think as players spend more time with the game they will likely come to the same conclusions, and I think the devs would do well to look at other games in the genre and figure out what makes them work. At least completely nuke the whole weapon leveling concept, replace it with weapons that change the behaviour of your cobun to allow greater skill expression rather than just flat stat upgrades. 啦嗒铛 Ratatan 从Ratatan刚出第一个预告的时候，我就已经开始关注了。作为啪嗒砰系列的粉丝，同时它也是我的第一款psp白月光的情况下，讲真，在索尼不怀好意的狙击下（指卡着Ratatan发售的节点发布Patapon 1+2重制版来分流系列粉丝，索尼罪大滔天），能看到当年的制作组重新聚在一起，这个ip以另一种方式重生，就已经是莫大的惊喜了。至于游戏质量，经历了三部做的越来越好的啪嗒砰，积攒了非常多游戏制作经验的制作组，作品质量肯定是可以相信的......吗？我们都说隔行如隔山，而团队从Patapon这一节奏型arpg转向肉鸽Ratatan的过程中，这种转专业的生疏感被进一步放大，从而使得目前的ea版本只能称得上一部普普通通，伤仲永的平庸作品（鉴于当前版本较早，团队也发布了相应的更新路线图，因此本评测仅针对目前刚刚发布的ea v0.5.5版本，未来还是值得期待与观望的）。 Ratatan与Patapon最大的共性，就是二者皆为节奏型的音游。制作组一脉相承地发挥了他们最大的洗脑节奏和音乐的优点。在几张地图内，多种风格迥异的bgm高密度展开，能保证你每一刻都在随着鼓点摇头晃脑。从海滩的悠闲，到丛林的原始，墓地的神秘。配合上小人咿呀咿呀的可爱音效，Ratatan生动地在这一方面诠释了什么叫做热闹与混乱。在此之上，制作组还简化了节奏指令，四个按键改为三个，每个动作的输入指令都变得非常简单，还提供了音游常见的下落条来辅助打节奏。相较于Patapon系列需要fever才能获取正常收益，一旦断联就会至少浪费三个四拍子行动时间的惩罚，对节奏和环境要求苛刻的特点，Ratatan对于断联无任何惩罚（甚至不会断fever），perfect（just！）与great（good）之间也没有什么显著的区别，这一系列适应现代玩家的简化操作都让初次接触该作品的新玩家对于它更加容易上手。如果是比较熟悉硬核的Patapon系列老玩家，游戏也提供了系列传统的四拍子输入和边框节奏。这样的锐意进取绝对不是什么坏改动，我也很高兴见到团队不墨守成规，勇于向现代化游戏思路迈进，吸引更多受众的表现。 但正如我在啪嗒砰1+2复刻版的评测中提到的，Patapon系列的最大魅力在于音画结合的艺术性表达。Ratatan在这两个方面都存在很大的问题，从而将本该成为最大优势的长板变为了平庸的中板，说它短板吧又不至于，不上不下，卡在这里了。 先来说音乐的问题。音宝们吵闹起来会稀释拍子节奏感的系列传统问题并没有得到解决，这个只是小问题。真正的大问题在于游戏为战斗和安全地区配置了不同的bgm，而没有任何的丝滑转场切换。我刚在一场战斗中幸存下来，配合bgm斗志昂扬的时刻，转眼间来到了下一个没怪的安全区域，于是安全的bgm又从头播放，强行打断了玩家的沉浸体验。待到你想去适应安全的bgm循环时，下一个门背后又突然刷出怪物，于是又突兀地从头切换至战斗bgm。我们说音游讲究的是连贯性，是一整场大关卡用一个洗脑循环的bgm从头贯穿到尾的舒畅感，而不是把音乐播放器放到兜里面跑步，没一会就摇一摇切歌，这也使得玩家还没热起来就时而被打断的情绪没法完全沉浸在音乐中，本作好听的bgm设计也在一定程度上失去了意义。 而音乐的问题相较于画面的问题而言，则真真正正只是小问题。先来问大家一个问题，Patapon为何要选择黑白画面为主要色调，只在必要的重点部分克制地使用颜色呢？在一个部队或者说军团大规模对战的平面2d游戏中，飞矢，流箭乱飞，魔法随处放，每个角色都形态迥异，想要保证画面在特效密集的同时保持干净整洁，就必须克制色调的使用，将体现差异的活留给形状。所以你能看到Patapon系列在军队大规模与敌方军队交战之时，尽管投枪，弓箭，魔法等各种不同攻击齐出，但整个的画面是干净的，是好看到可以当壁纸的。然而Ratatan彻底舍弃掉了这一优势。毫不加以节制的色彩调用，背景，人物和特效混在一起，让玩家在茫茫多的杂乱色彩中抓不住重点。也让武器装备以及敌人的形象在肉鸽游戏中毫无区分度，平庸地像是随处可见的类型。换句话说，一位在顶尖学府研究尖端科技的人才主动舍弃了推动业界发展的机会并去普通公司当了茫茫多大众上班族中的一员。上班族也并不算多差，只是对本可以扬名立万的它而言实在让人惋惜。 在肉鸽可玩性的部分，Ratatan稚嫩地像牙牙学语的婴儿一般。似乎是由于三部Patapon全部偏向于以arpg作为核心，团队不仅对于肉鸽没有什么经验，还保留了许多的arpg习惯在里面。对于一个2025年的肉鸽而言，关卡、地形和boss稀少重复；局外成长对游戏的影响占比过重：包括数值以及多个对强度有显著影响的核心机制，例如歌宝的最大数量；玩家在局内对于路线选择几乎没有什么可操作项，属性的卡牌基本是雨露均沾bd随缘。虽然游戏做了8种不同语音的英雄区分，但其差异化明显不足，每个英雄基本也就是固定携带的兵种配置不同。这让玩家基本也就是看哪个带的兵能装备的好武器多就用哪个。说到这个英雄，这也是Ratatan一个很奇怪的矛盾点：在战斗中，作为小兵的歌宝可以无限复活，拥有单独血条的英雄死亡游戏才会真正失败。英雄在游戏中虽然可以自由移动，但由于根本没有任何的攻击手段和增益作用，只能借由硬直来发出节奏指令，导致游戏中大部分的时间就是让歌宝们一窝蜂地冲上去普攻技能来回按，英雄躲在后面挂机就行了。甚至在一些输入指令来不及闪避的技能时，还必须放弃歌宝直接操纵英雄走位躲避。英雄唯一的攻击手段是在凑齐一定数量的同属性卡牌后，身边会刷新火球冰球等环绕物，可以造成对应的伤害或者冻结效果。但其伤害低效果差不说，英雄贴脸运球的收益与风险远不成正比，为了贪那一丢丢伤害而有概率吃到敌人的高威力技能完全是得不偿失。这一整个肉鸽的部分给人的感觉就只有青涩的矛盾。 总的来说，Ratatan是一款其存在就令我的情怀感到欣慰的作品。能看到这部作品成功落地，本身对我而言就是莫大的抚慰了。虽然游戏本身的质量实在是乏善可陈，但考虑到这是团队重组后的第一部作品，他们乐于听取玩家意见的态度，以及游戏还在ea阶段不断完善中，我是肯定不会给作品判死刑的。Patapon用了整整三部，五年的时间才登上同类作品的经典王座，相信在未来的某一天，成熟结果的Ratatan团队也一定可以为玩家们带来最初的感动，并带领可爱的歌宝们回到曾经到达过的最高的山峰。 There is a lot of effort put into this game, but its really in the wrong places. They wanted to make "patapon but with new stuff" - the roguelite aspect is definitely new, but its quite boring to play more than a few times. The art is extremely nice, and there are main characters who are really well made - but they are tied to classes, so if you have a character then your army is fixed, and vice-versa. Oh, and they give you no options what to bring with you, have 2 types of classes, and you can either have 66% have class A and 33% have class B, or vice versa. There is no customization apart from 1(!) slot on each patapon guy, and it boils down to putting whatever gives you the most stats. There are random stat modifiers on equipment, but its plain. They have reused a lot of old music/effects while making new ones - and they managed it quite well at times, like jungle one is great - but WHY do you put COUNTRY music in my japanese-rhythm-god-rpg-whatever game? On the other hand there is a crating system, exchange of resources, global upgrades, quests - they are well joined together, but still rather plain, and there is no much strategic depth to it. Just grind, upgrade base stats, repeat on the same levels. I would see it work, but in another game. One of my biggest gripes with actual bad game design is that the command timing is fixed, global and immutable - so WHY DO BOSSES ATTACK OUTSIDE OF COMMAND WINDOW? 80% of attacks I see start and end in the single window (including the wind up animation), so I literally have to guess when an attack happens. There are some exceptions, but with mini bosses this happens all the time. I see a lot of potential, but right now the game itself is just not very good. Patapon nostalgia doesn't help it enough. The pace of the development is not bad, and I believe in the Japanese spirit - its a lot of work still.

Okay I will admit, the music and graphics are alright. But when it comes to the gameplay, it is pretty mediocre at best. Like seriously, what were these devs thinking when they thought that... pressing 1 button... over & over again... is fun? Now you may make the argument of... "oh but you press different keys to do different commands." Yeah but you're still pressing 1 key at the end of the day. Or better yet, you're really only gonna be doing 2 different commands 'cause the other 2 are complete garbage. For guard, it may reduce damage but you're still gonna take damage. Like you're better off just using the command that gathers your troops so they can dodge the attacks. Or really you're gonna be doing that anyway 'cause for some reason, your troops don't automatically come back to you after they attack. Like they just stand still taking damage from the enemies 'cause they choose not to move unless you tell them to. Acting like robots. And if they're not taking damage, that's because they're too far away from the enemies in which you would have to command them to come to you so they could attack the enemies. And for the other command where you and your troops jump high in the air and stay up there for a long time? Yeah, this is straight up a filler mechanic. Like the devs knew that the gameplay was boring & repetitive, so they added this jump command to... "spice it up a bit"... And you know that's true 'cause you're really only going to be using this command during boss fights where the boss just decides to charge up a full screen attack out of nowhere. Like we're still gonna be having our troops move & attack most of the time devs. Also, to bash more on these devs, the troops with the arrows are extremely awful. Like instead of shooting arrows in a straight line, they choose to shoot them straight up in the air in hopes that it would come down and hit someone. And obviously, the devs knew that if they code them where they aim accurately at enemies, they could all shoot on 1 single enemy which could reduce their dps. So they decided to just make them have a fixed shot angle but still, why have them designed like this? Like you have no idea how annoying it is when they miss their shots 'cause they're either too far away or they're too dang close that the arrows just go behind them. Like why not just have them shoot straight? Oh what's that? Some enemies would spawn on some hills in which the arrows could hit against it? Freaking remove them then? Like my goodness. Now, you may say, "oh just make them use different weapons", but that's the thing. I can't make them use different weapons. They can only use bows & arrows for some reason unless I find a new weapon for them. But even then, I would have to grind for hours to get lucky enough to find said new weapons for them. And speaking of which, yeah why is this game so dang grindy? Like I may be 2 and a half hours in and barely unlocked anything, but with the amount of gear that I have yet to unlock, it kinda tells me that I'm gonna have to spend dozens of hours in this game, playing the same repetitive gameplay just to find some new gear even though I have a high chance of getting duplicates. Like what the heck is this nonsense? Also, to bash more on the gameplay, I really don't like how you only have 2 options to pick after clearing a level. Like gee man, for a game that is supposedly a roguelike, you guys really did make it easy for us to make a good build even though there's 4 different kinds of elements and we can only choose between 2 at a time. If we're lucky at least. But yeah man, it really is unfortunate how the game ended up like this. Especially considering that... in my humble opinion, I think them saying, "An intense battle unfolds with over 100 characters fighting in a massive melee" is a lure tactic. 'Cause clearly they're not talking about you playing with 100 ACTUAL characters 'cause there's only 8 in this game. They're talking about you and your minions battling it out against some enemies. But as of right now, I can only have like 10 minions at a time. And every battle I'm in only has like 20 enemies or so. So clearly they're talking about you having a whole bunch of minions fighting against a whole bunch of enemies in any given battle which I think is kinda disgusting. 'Cause not only is there a chance where this doesn't even happen, but the chance of this ACTUALLY happening is when you grinded a whole bunch of hours into the game to be able to have a whole bunch of minions and get far enough into a run to go up against a whole bunch of enemies. So for them to say that you could have massive battles but hide the fact that you have to grind dozens of hours first is extremely insulting. I love Patapon. I played every Patapon game on the PSP and was extremely excited at the announcement of this game. This is not Patapon. And that's perfectly fine, but it's not a good roguelite either. The grind is necessary; it took me 1 run to get to the third boss and 6 runs to get [i]past[/i] the third boss, and then I promptly died on the next world because of how little damage I was doing. [h3] Examples of why you [i]have[/i] to grind [/h3] [list] [*] you grind for weapons, both legendary and not - because upgrading requires you to feed fodder weapons into your good ones [*] you grind for each individual character - because each one has separate goals/challenges you do to get rewards [*] you grind bosses and minibosses alike - because each one drops 1 out of 2 types of material you use to craft weapons [*] you grind for donuts and candy - these are used to upgrade stuff like health or unlocking blueprints for crafting weapons [*] you just have to grind levels - because there's a quest board and that seems to be the only way you can get chocolate which is used to unlock things [/list] As you can probably tell, it's unfortunately very grind heavy, and the game feels like it's disrespecting my time. Even if you have the best foresight and make all the right commands to avoid enemy attacks, they eventually will kill you if you don't do enough damage. It's also not a pick-up-and-play type of game; this is a sit-down-and-commit-for-1-hour type of game and I feel like that's not reflective of a players time and commitment these days. [h3] Gameplay [/h3] There is no campaign, and story is extremely sparse. You get some dialogue here and there in a way that's meant to be mysterious: "Looks like someone beat everything here" but it's completely ruined by the announcement of the Dark Ratatans in big bold letters, and trailers highlighting them. The bulk, and only, gameplay, is just the roguelite runs where you progress through multiple levels, beating enemies and bosses and picking up randomized powerups to make your build. It's reminiscent of Hades or Slay the Spire or any other roguelite game that has adopted this style of leveling. I'm not saying that's bad, but I am saying it's not a new concept. [h3] Combat [/h3] The combat feels... messy. Which is unfortunate because that's the entire game. Enemies and bosses don't seem to go at the same rhythm as you do or are always a little ahead of your commands, so even though you see an attack coming, you can't get away in time because you're still inputting commands to run away. Again, this is not Patapon (unfortunately). The game actually wants you to just forget your Cobun (the little guys) and just save yourself, this makes all the commands feel obsolete except for Attack, Hustle skills and Jump (because it makes your character stay in the air for a brief time). Guarding feels like a waste of time because they never guard in time, making you waste a turn of just standing there taking hits. The enemies run around and get past your line of defense and aim only for your character which seems to support the theory that you're really not supposed to care about the life and death of your Cobun, because they do come back to life if they die. There's the single attack theory in games, where if I can just win with a single type of attack, why would I need to press anything else? 1 hour into a run and I find myself staring at the screen blankly, pressing commands for Attack, Fall in (follow me) and Hustle Skill 1, possibly in that order, repeatedly. There's not a lot of joy to be gained to be honest, but a lot of frustration, when dealing with bosses that have obvious DPS checks (like Roshambo driving you to a corner if you don't kill it fast enough), and especially frustrating when you're a millisecond off of dodging an attack only to be hit before your command even registers. [h3] Art [/h3] Here's the thing, I think the game is incredibly cute. The designs are good, I like the different characters, the way they move, and how different they sound. The colours are extremely charming and cohesive and the Cobun surprisingly mesh well with the extremely detailed environments. I think this game looks amazing, but it's not enough for me to want to keep playing. [h3] Music / Sound Design [/h3] This is kind of the important part for a rhythm game, but I will say it doesn't feel that important in this game. You press the commands in time with the beat and everything is [i]supposed[/i] to move at that beat, but it doesn't feel like it. It feels more like you're confined to this beat, that you're the only one with this restraint while the enemy runs around without caring that you can only move every other 4/4 beat. The chanting is in-line with Patapon's, in that your Cobun says the sound cues with the buttons you press, but legally distinct from Patapon so they don't go "Pata Pata Pata Pon", they go "Rata Rata Ratatan". This is extremely nitpicky of me, but I think the sounds are a little too aggressive and sharp. Patapon has deeper sounds that felt soothing (and echoey 'PON's felt nice to hear) but in Ratatan, with the combination of the bells, the tambourines, the RATATA, it feels overwhelming at best and headache inducing at worst. It is catchy-ish; I think it has to be since that's kind of the only thing you're listening to the entire run, just different variations of the same song. [h3] Ending Comments [/h3] Overall, I wish this game was better. There's a lot of micro-aggressions in this game that make me more frustrated than anything. I start up the game after a brief period of not playing because I'm feeling nostalgic and I can remember the songs in my head, but once I start playing I remember why I stopped. To be honest... I think it might be better to just get the Patapon bundle (though I don't know if that ported over well at all, so look at the reviews there) because I feel like the developers forgot that we didn't really play Patapon for the combat, but for the puzzley aspect, the feel-good soothing sounds of the Pata and the Pons, and for the unique style of gameplay. This is Patapon but whittled down to a generic roguelite that didn't put much thought past "combat, but no strategy".
